title: Prospective evaluation of ex-vivo confocal laser endomicroscopy for immediate quality control of stereotactic brain biopsies.
summary:
Background: For deep-seated brain lesions, a stereotactic biopsy is performed using a fine needle to obtain small tissue samples for precise diagnostic assessment. Because surgeons cannot visualize the needle tip directly within the tissue, there is a risk of sampling non-diagnostic scar or margin tissue. Conventional intraoperative checks such as frozen section examinations consume valuable tissue and extend anesthesia time.   

Study Objective: This study evaluates an advanced laser imaging device (confocal laser endomicroscopy, ZEISS CONVIVO). The objective is to determine whether extracted specimens can be reliably assessed directly in the operating room within a few minutes to confirm representative tumor tissue. This aims to minimize unnecessary sampling passes and avoid repeat interventions.   

Procedure: The surgical procedure is conducted entirely according to the clinical standard of care. Patients receive an intravenous fluorescent dye (sodium fluorescein) prior to sampling to highlight cells under laser light. Immediately following excision, the tissue core is placed outside the body (ex-vivo) onto the laser microscope probe and scanned for one to two minutes. The tissue is neither damaged nor consumed by the imaging process and is immediately forwarded to routine neuropathology for definitive examination.
conditions: Contrast-enhancing intracranial lesions with blood-brain barrier disruption and an indication for stereotactic biopsy under radiological suspicion of a brain tumor (e.g., high-grade glioma, brain metastasis, or primary CNS lymphoma).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Clinical indication for stereotactic biopsy of an intracranial space-occupying lesion.   Radiological suspicion of a brain tumor (e.g., glioma, brain metastasis, lymphoma).   Confirmed contrast enhancement of the target lesion on preoperative MRI (reflecting blood-brain barrier breakdown necessary for sodium fluorescein uptake).Written informed consent provided by the patient.
Exclusion criteria:
Known hypersensitivity or allergy to sodium fluorescein.   
Renal insufficiency (GFR < 30 ml/min) or severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh stage B or C).   
Pregnancy or breastfeeding.   
Lack of capacity to give informed consent.
